recognize_zh: 箭頭所指的骨髓細胞胞質內有數顆大而圓、紫紅色的粗大包涵顆粒，遠大於一般嗜天青顆粒，是融合而成的巨大顆粒（pseudo-Chédiak-Higashi granules），常見於AML或MDS。
features: Arrowed myeloid cell with a large nucleus and fine chromatin containing several large round purple-red cytoplasmic granules
Giant granules markedly larger than normal azurophilic granules, clustered at one pole of the cytoplasm
Adjacent blast with high N:C ratio, fine chromatin and deeply basophilic cytoplasm without granules
Nearby myelocyte/promyelocyte with oval eccentric nucleus and pale granular cytoplasm
Background red cells without significant abnormality
describe_en: Smear shows an immature myeloid cell (arrow) with fine nuclear chromatin whose cytoplasm contains several large, round, purple-red granules considerably larger than ordinary azurophilic granules. An adjacent blast with basophilic agranular cytoplasm and a more mature granulocytic precursor are also present. Findings are consistent with pseudo-Chédiak-Higashi granules, an acquired abnormality typically seen in AML or myelodysplastic neoplasms rather than inherited Chédiak-Higashi syndrome.

ddx.vs: The inherited disorder shows giant granules in mature neutrophils, lymphocytes and other lineages of most cells in a child with albinism, rather than in occasional leukemic precursors.
Auer rods are slender needle-shaped pink-red inclusions, whereas pseudo-Chédiak-Higashi granules are large round globules.
Döhle bodies are pale blue cytoplasmic patches and toxic granules are fine dark granules in mature neutrophils, not large round granules in immature cells.
Alder-Reilly granules are diffuse dark lilac granules in all neutrophils in mucopolysaccharidosis, not a few giant globules in blasts.
